data.narrative:
Magrathea Metals is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Alex Grant and Jacob Brown that has raised $100M+. The broader sector peer set comprises 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, a sufficiently narrow peer cohort of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within Climate & Energy does not exist with three or more datapoints, limiting application of median valuation methods.

The analysis applies stage-progression methodology, using the $100M total raised as a proxy for implied entry valuation. Applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields $200M. This single-method approach forms the analytical foundation given the scarcity of tightly clustered peer data.

The triangulated valuation range is $170M to $230M, with a median of $200M. This range reflects the stage-progression result plus and minus a reasonable confidence band. Key uncertainties stem from (1) the absence of narrow-set peer multiples to corroborate or refine the step-up assumption, and (2) reliance on total raised as a valuation proxy rather than disclosed pricing data. Further diligence on portfolio company chemistries, capex burn, and technical risk profile would be warranted before commitment.
